criteria.statement: A requirement row whose criteria names an id that no criterion row of the table has fails with unknown-criterion.

A requirement row with both proofs or neither fails, an agreed difference that does not name ADR-0083 fails, an agreed difference on an id that is not a sub-id fails with difference-on-parent, and a sub-id whose parent is not in the fixed list fails.

An id both in open and a row fails, and each id of the fixed in-scope list that is neither in open nor a row fails with missing-requirement. The list is B17.01 to B21.05 without B19.03, A01 to A18, B01 to B13, C01 to C08, D01 to D12, X01, X02, X04, X05, X06, G03, G04, G05, G06 and G10.
coverage/milestone-3.json passes unchanged, and a table with no requirements section is checked as before.
The table holds an agreed-difference row under its own sub-id for B17.01/utc, B17.06/head-unit, B18.07/model-call, B20.01/zones, X04/zone and G06/midnight, and none of them closes its parent.
A unit that declares fewer criteria than the plan gives it fails with below-plan, and a requirement row whose criteria differ from its planned ids fails with differs-from-plan.
A requirement row whose criteria all carry phoneSession or noAutomatedProof fails with no-named-test, unless the row has phoneSessionOnly with a reason.

A range holding a WORKOUT, a RACE_A, a RACE_B, a RACE_C, a NOTE and a HOLIDAY lists the four planning rows and only those, each with id, date, name, category, coachCreated, durationSeconds and load equal to the fixture.
With coachCreatedOnly true the same range lists only the coach-created rows, and a coach-tagged race is listed and still has coachCreated true.
A row with no moving_time has no durationSeconds key, a row with no icu_training_load has no load key, and a row with moving_time 0 lists durationSeconds 0.
An entry with no name lists with no name key, and the rest of the range lists normally.
A reversed range, a range of 367 days and a malformed date each answer with their refusal and make no read call, and a range of exactly 366 days is read.
An omitted newest reads up to the phone's day: with the phone clock at 00:30 on 1998-09-08 in Pacific/Auckland, newest is 1998-09-08.
The REST request still sends no category, and listEventsDoesNotFilterAwayMovedIdentities passes unchanged.
The list tool's description no longer says Filters to WORKOUT category only, and names workouts and races, races never changeable and coachCreatedOnly.
Every case of serializer-cases.json, regenerated by running npm's serializer at d192cb97, serializes to npm's description and movingTime byte for byte, or is refused where npm refuses it.
The 15-minute case with a repeat followed by a step in the same section has a blank line after the repeat block and a movingTime of 900.
A ride with 41 steps, 21 repeats, a 121-character name or label, 1501 W, 201 %FTP, or a ramp with one bound is refused as invalid_workout with no review and no calendar write.

Every case of serializer-cases.json, given as a ride add, builds a request body whose description and moving_time equal npm's description and movingTime byte for byte, and every case npm refuses is refused. A ride whose serialized duration is 0 seconds is refused as invalid_workout.
A Load of 41.6 is sent as icu_training_load 42 for a ride and a strength session, a Load of -1 is refused for both, and an add with no Load sends no icu_training_load.

A strength session of 37.5 minutes is sent with moving_time 2250, its trimmed effort and its description joined by one blank line, its trimmed name, and its own Load, and fractional minutes round to whole seconds as Math.round does.

A whitespace-only name, a 121-character name, a whitespace-only effort, a past date, a missing or empty field, a 4001-character description, and durations of 0, -5, infinity, 10^16 and 0.001 minutes are each refused before any write, and a whitespace-only description is accepted.
A ride and a strength session parsed from one input list keep their own type, name, date, duration, Load and description.
A body built with a CalendarWriteID carries category WORKOUT, that uid, external_id cycling-coach:<uid>, the coach tag, and no other field than the payload's.

An edit patch naming only the date, the name, durationSeconds, the description, trainingLoad or a native structure builds a request body with that one field: start_date_local at T00:00:00, the trimmed name, moving_time, description, icu_training_load rounded to a whole number, or workout_doc.

Authored steps in a patch's structure send the serializer's description and moving_time for every case of serializer-cases.json npm accepts, and no workout_doc. A native workout_doc is sent unchanged and becomes the desired structure. A description alone sends only the description and sets the desired structure to none, unless the description equals the current one after line endings are normalized.

A patch with no field, an unknown field, a past destination, a name of 121 characters or blank after trimming, an unreal date, a duration that is not a positive whole number of seconds, a 4001-character description, a negative Load, a structure that is not an object, or authored steps the serializer refuses is refused. Today's date, a 120-character name, an empty description, one second and a Load of 0 are accepted.
applied(to:) changes exactly the fields a patch names, alone or together, normalizes a patched description's line endings, and leaves every other field of the snapshot as it was.

CalendarEvent.snapshot of a list row read through the REST client holds its date, name, moving_time, icu_training_load, description with normalized line endings and workout_doc as normalized JSON, an absent or null value stays absent, and an event without a calendar date has no snapshot.

The calendar client writes only through write(_:), beside fetchEvent and listEvents, and chatCreateBody is gone. An add is one POST to events/bulk with upsert=true, upsertOnUid=false and updatePlanApplied=false whose body is a one-element array holding the add's CalendarPayload body; an edit is one PUT of its WorkoutPatch body and a delete is one DELETE, with no read of the target first.

A 2xx edit answer is saved with its decoded event, a 2xx add answer is saved with its list's one event, an add answer whose list holds no event or more than one, or that is not a list, is lost as unreadable, a 2xx delete is saved with no event, a 404, 422 or 503 keeps its status, a timeout is lost in transport, a canceled request is lost as canceled, and an undecodable 2xx body is lost as unreadable. Each write sends its request once.

The old path's add of a ride or a strength session sends today's body, with its uid, its cycling-coach:<uid> external_id, the coach tag and no moving_time, Load or workout_doc, as the bulk array's one element, and its update and delete refuse a race, an athlete-owned workout, a past workout and a move into the past with today's codes from CalendarWriteOperation before any write.

The old path's approvals keep their outcomes on the new call: a saved add is applied once, a refused or lost add leaves the pending review with the unconfirmed notice, and a lost answer is confirmed by reading, for adds, edits and deletes.

make live-seed adds the four entries that are never targets (an athlete-owned workout, a coach-tagged race, a note with an empty name, because intervals.icu refuses a note with no name, and a past workout) and the coach-created future targets T1, T2, K on T1's date, T3, T4 and T5, dated from the day it runs; a rerun adds only the missing entries and keeps an edited one; and make live-calendar lists each seeded entry once through the app's calendar decoding with its category, name, duration and Load.

A 15-minute repeat ride and a strength session added through write(_:) with a CalendarWriteID read back with the sent date, category, type, name, description, duration, Load, coach tag and the external_id cycling-coach:<id> exactly as sent, intervals.icu parses the ride's steps into a workout that lasts its reviewed 900 seconds, so the step after the repeat is not folded into it, and any field intervals.icu stores differently fails the check unless intervals-rewrites.json lists that rewrite.

The same add sent twice through write(_:) is saved twice as the same event with the add's external_id, and the add's 366-day window holds exactly that one event (gate M2-G1); a calendar that adds a second event fails the check.

Each field of a workout patch changed alone (date, name, Load, duration, description and authored steps) reads back as the patch applied to the snapshot before it, keeps the external_id, and applying the patch to the read-back snapshot changes nothing, apart from the rewrites intervals-rewrites.json lists.
A DELETE answers saved, a second DELETE of the same id and a PUT to it each answer httpStatus(404), and a GET of it answers 404.
With a key whose athlete differs from the seed ledger's, or a ledger that names no athlete, the check stops before any calendar request and adds no ledger row.
The run fails when a file of its run folder holds the key, checked with LiveRunFolder.files(containing:), and passes when none does.

An add moved by PUT 30 days later and another moved 200 days later, outside its 366-day window, are each sent again through write(_:) and each leaves one event with its first id; the window read finds the 30-day one on its new date before the resend, and the log records the date each resend left.
An add whose body carries an unknown category answers httpStatus or lost through write(_:), never saved, leaves no event, and the log records the status and body of the answer.
Each transition maps every stage to the documented next stage or refuses with wrongStage, every (stage, DriveStart) pair gives the documented NextStep, and no settle leaves the stage running.
Every change is in exactly one of finished, remaining and the stage's send attempt after every transition, and a finished change never returns to remaining.
answered with a lost answer gives readFirst, and settled with seen while work remains gives waiting(tryAgain(.settled)), so the run stops even when the change is found.
A refused answer puts the change back at the head of remaining with tryAgain(.refused(id, status)) for 400, 401, 403, 404 and 429.
differences(from:) names each changed field alone and ignores a change in server metadata or an equivalent representation, trailing whitespace and a moving_time equal after rounding.
isApplied(on:) is true exactly when applying the patch to the current snapshot changes nothing, an upgraded edit included.
The stored value round-trips, and a value with a change in two places or two changes at one position fails to decode.
sending(at:seen:) finishes each seen add as seen on the calendar, never with a Receipt, starts the send attempt of the first change not seen, and gives completed when every remaining change is seen.
nextStep(_:summarySaved:) gives publish for a completed or canceled review whose summary is not saved, and idle once it is.

OperationID.workoutReview encodes to the same workoutChangeSet:<ulid>:<rev> string as before, an old string decodes, and the build-2bbe2ee seed keeps its memory, history and consent after the rename while its open proposal closes as ask the coach again.

The minted-in-one-file rule fails each of its five patterns in a package file outside the owner, passes them in the owner, and passes ReviewReceipt( and other names that only contain Receipt or SendAttempt.

An add, an edit and a delete each send exactly one request through CalendarWriter.send with the reviewed body, and no other request: an add is one bulk upsert of a one-element array carrying external_id cycling-coach:<id>, an edit is a PUT of the patch's fields, and a delete is a DELETE, with no read first.

classify gives saved for a create whose answer event carries its external_id and the payload's date, name, type and description, with intervals.icu's own Load and derived workout_doc allowed, and lost for another external_id or other content, never reading the answer's uid; an update naming another event is lost; a DELETE with 2xx is saved and with 404 gone; 400, 401, 403, 404 and 429 to an add or edit are refused; a 500, a 502, a timeout, an unreadable body and a cancellation are lost.

settle of an add reads its 366-day window from 183 days before its date once and gives seen for one event carrying its external_id on its date or another day, notSaved for none and readFailed for two; of an edit, seen when the patch is applied after the rewrites intervals-rewrites.json lists, else notSaved; of a delete, gone for 404 and notSaved when present; any failed read gives readFailed.

On the live test calendar, with the answer dropped by the check's session, an add settles as seen, an edit as seen through isApplied(on:), and a delete as gone from a GET of the deleted id, each with no request other than its one write and the settle read.

The old card shows the same buttons, labels, order and decisions in every state, the storage-unavailable card's retry-read button included, and every app test and UI proof of the old card passes with only names changed.
Each outcome the old path produces gives the same notice key and values as before.
blocked(.reviewedBeforeUpgrade) gives workouts.blocked.reviewedBeforeUpgrade, and wrongAction gives no notice and leaves the controls live.

Delivery gives no control before acknowledge(); after it the controls are armed with the stage's allowedControls, or none when the stage allows none, and a token from an earlier head or an earlier delivery is not admitted.

ReviewProjection orders cards by position across finished changes, the send attempt and the remaining work, with each card's progress, and shows a completed or canceled head read-only with no control.

Each new body (workoutReview, reviewPreparing, reviewOutcome) round-trips through the SwiftData store at body version 6, and a Milestone 3 build, whose body version is 5, skips each version-6 row as newerVersion before it reads the kind and reads every other row.

When two ledgers append after the same head, exactly one append lands and the other gets headMoved with the new head; over 200 runs in parallel tasks no chain has two records after one head, over one SwiftDataRecordLog, over two logs opened separately on one store directory, and over the in-memory store.
Two ModelContainerHandle.deviceLocal(directory:) opens of one directory return the same handle, and another directory gets another handle.
An append whose save fails leaves the head unchanged and reports a storage failure, not headMoved.
reviewHead returns the newest workoutReview of the chat and folds its clock, so the next record sorts after it.
A reviewOutcome written on one device is read on another, the first per review winning; a workoutReview and a reviewPreparing are not.
The review-chain-only rule fails WorkoutReviewBody( and ReviewPreparingBody( in a package file outside Records/ReviewChain.swift and the three codec files, and passes each of those four files.

A mixed request of two adds, one edit and one delete drafts four changes with zero calendar writes and zero review records, each payload equal to the one 2.2 or 2.3 builds for the same input, and two same-named workouts on one date are each identified by their event.

At 00:30 on 1998-09-08 in Pacific/Auckland, an edit or delete of a workout dated 1998-09-08 and a ride or strength add on that date are drafted; the same on 1998-09-07, an athlete-owned workout, a race, a note and a move to 1998-09-07 are refused with no draft; a workout with or without a paired activity is judged the same.
An edit and a delete of one event in one set, or two edits of it, are refused with no draft.
Kept workouts list the untargeted WORKOUT entries of each affected date and leave out the targets, and the moved workout's original date is not read.
An unreadable target refuses with targetUnreadable and drafts nothing.
get_pending_workout_changes with only a draft answers none, and for a waiting review lists item ids apart from event ids.
The old path still refuses the same targets with the same codes at approval and in recovery.
A test turn that prepares and then replies commits one review at revision 1; before the reply ends pending answers none and the desk's snapshot gives no card.

A turn that prepares and then fails, is stopped, runs out of tool rounds, or loses that generation to a provider retry commits nothing, stores turnDidNotFinish on its settlement, and shows workouts.notPrepared under the turn apart from the turn's own notice.
A turn that saves a memory fact and then fails after preparing keeps the fact, shows the saved-but-not-verified notice, and shows the review notice joined to the saved-information text.

A kill after the claim and before the marker settles as processEnded with no review notice; a kill during the preparation reads, including reads that follow an unreadable request, or after the reply and before the commit leaves nothing approvable and shows workouts.notPrepared; a kill during a revision's reads leaves the waiting review unchanged and shows workouts.notPrepared; a kill after the commit and before turnSettled finds the commit on relaunch, shows the card, and the turn has no review notice.

Revising one of four changes keeps the other three byte for byte with their ids and uids at revision 2, a revised rename keeps the earlier patch's duration, description and authored steps, and a revision that changes an item's action, workout or sport, or changes nothing, is refused.
A replacement after two finished changes keeps both as finished at the next revision.
Once revision 2 commits, the chat's delivery admits no token minted for revision 1.
A revise against an old base or a complete set while a review waits is refused and the waiting review is unchanged; preparation against a running or unconfirmed head is refused.
Eleven minutes and an unrelated turn after the commit, pending returns the waiting review unchanged.

A revise naming an event id as an item id, an edit naming an item id as its event, and a revise naming an item id of an earlier review each draft nothing, replace the attempt's earlier draft, and leave the waiting review unchanged; a model step with more than one preparation refuses all of them, and the attempt settles refused with nothing committed.
Before presented(ref) the snapshot has no control; after it the controls are armed(approveOrCancel, token).

presentationFailed(ref) leaves no control and a token minted before it is not admitted; showAgain(ref) makes a new delivery with no control until it is presented; a presented for an older head or delivery arms nothing.

A set whose last change targets a workout that lost coach provenance after review gives blocked(coachOnly); a race gives blocked(workoutOnly), and a target dated in the past or an edit moved into the past gives blocked(pastProtected).
A deleted target gives blocked(cannotVerify), and the verdict carries no refreshed values, even beside a changed target.

An edit or delete target dated 1998-09-07, prepared at 23:30 that day in Pacific/Auckland, gives blocked(pastProtected) when preflight runs at 00:30 on 1998-09-08 there, while UTC is still on 1998-09-07.
An add dated 1998-09-07, prepared at 23:30 that day in Pacific/Auckland, gives blocked(pastProtected) when preflight runs at 00:30 on 1998-09-08 there.
A different athlete's key after review gives blocked(accountChanged) before any calendar read or write.

A target whose duration went from 60 to 90 minutes gives changed naming that target and duration, with every remaining target's current values and the kept workouts; date, name, description, Load and structure changed alone are each named alone; a change made on intervals.icu after preflight and before the write is not detected.

A change only in server metadata gives clear; each rewrite intervals-rewrites.json lists gives clear, except that preflight names every Load difference, and isApplied(on:) reads the rewritten save as applied, while the same field changed in a way the rule does not explain is named.
One unreadable target, an unreadable kept-workout day or an unreadable add window gives unchecked with no write.

A remaining add whose external_id is in its 366-day window is in clear's seen list and not among the kept workouts, on its own date and 30 days later or earlier; one outside the window or matching only by uid is not seen; two events carrying it give unchecked; each window is read once.
Eligibility is judged before difference: a target that both changed and became a race gives blocked(workoutOnly), and every earlier check decides over every later one.
After a target changed from 60 to 90 minutes, the refreshed review is one revision higher, the edited target's reviewed duration is 90 minutes, and its card still asks for 75.
The refreshed review's notice names the workout, says it changed in intervals.icu, gives 60 to 90 minutes, and says nothing was changed; after finished work it says nothing else was changed.
Date, name, duration, description, training load and workout steps each changed alone give their own sentence, and two changed targets give two sentences.
The kept workouts of the refreshed review are the ones read at preflight, not the ones read at preparation.

Approving the mixed review after another turn sends four requests in card order, each equal to its reviewed change, saves four Receipts and a completed outcome, keeps the unrelated 45-minute workout, and adds no model request; a refreshed review approved with its new token runs its changes; the live-calendar desk run checks the same on the test account against a calendar fake.

The claim is the review head at the first preflight read; when the claim's append fails, the approval gives storageUnavailable, nothing is read or sent, the head stays, and the same token then runs the review.

Each write request leaves while the record holding its send attempt is the head; when the append of attempt k fails for an add, an edit or a delete as change k, no request k is sent and the head stays at the record of change k-1.

A renewed, consumed, canceled or other-chat token sends nothing and saves nothing; after a refreshed review the old token sends nothing and its outcome names the newer revision; a wrong action sends nothing and leaves the token usable.

A double tap, two concurrent deliveries of one token, and two desks over one store whose head reads are held until both have read each save one running claim with no sending attempt, run seven chain records, give staleControl to the loser and send four requests.

Cancel before approval is saved and published before its outcome returns and sends nothing, and after a relaunch its token sends and saves nothing; a renewed or consumed Cancel token saves nothing; cancel after two saved changes keeps both Receipts; approve and cancel raced save one head that the shown outcome matches.

An add first and a last target that lost coach provenance, is gone, is unreadable or belongs to another account, or an add dated before the phone's today, gives zero write requests and saves the blocked or could-not-check stage; a blocked review offers Cancel alone and refuses Approve.

After two saved changes and a refused third, no fourth request is sent, the outcome stops with two saved cards and the refused one, and the review keeps the two finished changes apart from the two remaining.

For an add, an edit and a delete whose answer is lost, the run sends no second request; a change the immediate read finds finishes as seen on the calendar or no longer on it, never with a Receipt; one not found returns to the remaining work; a failed read leaves it unconfirmed.

twoDesksApproveOnceRunOnce, changedTargetBeforeApprovalWritesNothing and unownedTargetWritesNothing each fail on each of 20 runs with their defect planted: a claim that skips the head check at the desk's claim call site, differences(from:) returning no difference, and eligibility returning no refusal.
After a completed run, a relaunched desk answers the old token's Approve and Cancel with staleControl and sends and saves nothing.

The run holds one athlete lease from the claim until the drive ends and ends it finished after a completed, stopped or unconfirmed run and failed after a storage failure; a host that ends the lease mid-run leaves the change in flight unconfirmed, the lease interrupted, and the saved head's resume step a settle of that change.

Each execution row of the crash table stops the old drive for good at its point, and recover() on a new desk over the same store leaves the expected head with the exact request count, with no request or append from the stopped drive after its point; each row with a request runs for an add, an edit and a delete, and the landed add includes one moved 30 days later.

A failed append at each append of the mixed run, the summary included, ends the drive with a storage failure whose snapshot shows the storage notice and no control, and the next recover() resumes from the last saved head.
An unconfirmed change is read again at every recover() call and at Check again; a read that finds it ends the unconfirmed state, and a read that fails writes no record and leaves the token usable.
Check again with a stale token, or in any other stage, reads nothing.
Two recover() calls at once, on one desk or on two, or a kill inside one, end in the same head as one call, and recovery finds each chat that holds a review chain once.

A second desk's recover() during a live send of an add leaves one chain with no two records after one head and one calendar event for the add, with one POST for that change, and the first desk stops on headMoved when its answer is released.
Relaunch and device restart more than ten minutes after a review was prepared restore the same review and revision, and the same control set once the view presents it again, with no model request.

holdsBoundWork is true for a waiting, running or unconfirmed head and for a preparing attempt, and false for a completed or canceled head, a canceled unconfirmed change included; the changes stream names the chat whose card a recover changed.

After two saved changes and a stopped run, Try again reads the remaining targets before any request and sends only the third and fourth changes; the first two are never sent again, on the same desk, after a relaunch, or after a replacement that keeps them finished.

When a remaining target changed before Try again, nothing is sent; the notice names the change, keeps the two Receipts and says nothing else was changed, and a new approval of the refreshed review follows.

After a refused add, Try again reads the add's window before any request; an event carrying the add's external_id finishes it as seen on the calendar with no request, and otherwise it is sent once through the bulk upsert with the same CalendarWriteID.
The final calendar equals the reviewed outcome.
A Try again token that is stale, consumed, canceled or from an earlier revision sends nothing, and a double tap or two desks with one barrier give one claim and one request per remaining change.

A completed review's outcome note lists every change after the turn that committed it, after a refresh, a reopen, New conversation (in the archived conversation) and a relaunch, with no live card and no control.
A cancel after partial work keeps every saved line and the may-have-been-saved line of the canceled unconfirmed change, and no later recover reads that change.

A second device shows the synced outcome note with no card and no control, holds no bound work, and turns a token from the first device into a stale control; the first outcome of a review by clock wins in any order.

After New conversation a waiting review shows once, at the top, with placement preparedEarlier and the line "Prepared earlier", and can be approved; a review prepared after New conversation stays after its turn.
A delete whose target was already gone, by a 404 answer or by the settle read after a lost answer, reads "no longer on the calendar" and never as saved.
After Cancel in waiting(unconfirmed), a complete preparation commits a new review at revision 1, the canceled change keeps its may-have-been-saved note, and its target is never read.
The open-review and unknown-write scenarios each upgrade as stated, once, and a second run plans nothing.
When the second upgrade append fails, a second run upgrades the rest, and every item is upgraded exactly once.

An unknown add found by its external_id finishes as seen on the calendar, also when the Milestone 2 single create made it; one not found becomes waiting(approval(.interruptedBeforeWriting)), and approving it gives preflight clear and one bulk upsert with the Milestone 2 external_id.
An unknown write made on another device, with no payload here, or with no CalendarWriteID, gets no review.
An upgraded edit or delete asked to run again blocks with reviewedBeforeUpgrade.
The completed scenario plans nothing, and its records stay as they are.

The carried section lists the single-change test files, and every test function and XCUITest method in them has one row with a statement and either replacement tests outside the listed files or the ADR that retires it.

The coverage checker fails a carried row whose replacement test is missing or lives in a listed file, and a test of a listed file that has no row; once a listed file is deleted its rows stand on their replacements alone.
Each test written for a single-change requirement that had no Milestone 4 test passes against the desk or the review tools.
For a connected athlete the tool offer holds the two review tools and none of the four old ones, the prompt has no one-mutation rule, and no prompt text or skill names intervals_create_workout.
The source holds none of the deleted single-change names, and check-source fails when one returns, through a constructor, an inferred .init or an old tool name.

A build-6833d90f open review shows ask the coach again with no control, and an unknown write shows an unconfirmed change that is read again at becameActive; both open offline and recover once the calendar can be read.
In the completed scenario the note of the applied write and the note of the canceled unknown write read the same after the upgrade as before, with no control.
An old turn with stored calendar-write counts still shows its notice.
Every carried row stands on its replacements once the listed files are deleted, and no criterion row cites a deleted file.
Two becameActive events in one process each read an unconfirmed change through Coach, and the second read finds it.
The athlete switch is refused while a review waits, runs or is unconfirmed, and allowed once it is completed or canceled.

The card shows each control set's buttons, each waiting for its token, the storage-unavailable card shows the notice with no usable control, and the card appears after the reply ends, never during it.

In make live-coach, after its seeded targets T1, T2 and K are each found once, the mixed request on T1, T2 and two adds prepares one workout review of those four changes in one prepare_workout_changes call with no calendar write, and every model call is admitted against the $10 cap in LIVE_LOGS/spend.tsv before it is sent.
"Make Thursday easier" revises one change: the review is at revision 2 and the other three changes keep their ids and actions.
An explicit "replace all of it" replaces the set: the replacement names the waiting review's setId and revision as its base, and revision 2 holds only the new changes, none of revision 1.
Before a revision or a replacement the coach calls get_pending_workout_changes before prepare_workout_changes.
An unrelated message prepares nothing and leaves the waiting review unchanged.
Cancel of the waiting review answers canceled, makes zero calendar requests, and leaves no review waiting.

With no review waiting, moving the seeded race gives a prepare_workout_changes result that carries the race refusal (not_a_workout, the workoutOnly ineligibility), the turn shows workouts.notPrepared, and no review waits.
The coach run fails when a file of its run folder holds either Keychain key, checked with LiveRunFolder.files(containing:), and passes when none does.

requirements.statement: The calendar list's omitted end date is the phone's day, not UTC today.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0083 makes the phone's time zone decide today for every read, so the list's omitted end date is the phone's day.

requirements.statement: Delivery of an approved ride to a Garmin or Wahoo head unit is not verified.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0083 leaves the head-unit half of B17.06 unverified, because the test account has no Garmin or Wahoo link.

requirements.statement: No model call judges an unfinished calendar request, and the reply's text is not held back.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0083 drops npm's extra model call for an unfinished request, and replies keep streaming while the card appears after the reply ends.

requirements.statement: Eligibility uses the phone's day when the phone's and the athlete's time zones differ.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0083 makes the phone's time zone decide today for every calendar change, so B20.01's different-zones check is an agreed difference.

requirements.statement: The athlete's civil date is the phone's day, not a date kept apart from the phone clock.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0083 makes the phone's time zone decide today for every read and change, with no note when the athlete's zone differs.

requirements.statement: An approval across the athlete's midnight is judged at the phone's midnight.
requirements.agreedDifference: ADR-0083 makes the phone's time zone decide today, so G06's athlete-midnight journey is an agreed difference.

requirements.statement: The calendar list holds WORKOUT and race events with their fields and coach ownership, keeps unknown values apart from zero, reads only real ranges of at most 366 days, and a listed race stays refused for any edit or delete.

A strength session carries its date, trimmed name, rounded duration, trimmed effort, description and optional Load, refuses blank, out-of-range or unsafe values before any write, and keeps its own fields beside a ride in one list.
An approved ride is parsed by intervals.icu as reviewed: its duration, steps and repeat block read back from the live calendar as sent.
Each field of an add or an edit reaches the request as reviewed, and Load is sent as a whole-number estimate that intervals.icu may recalculate.
Present absent activity pairing for an otherwise eligible workout → make no inference that the workout is incomplete.
Present activity pairing → apply the accepted restrictions without introducing a completion-based prohibition.

One saved set holds every addition, edit and deletion, with no calendar write during preparation, bound to the account, chat and reviewed targets, and nothing is approvable until the whole set is committed at the end of the reply.

Revising chosen items or replacing the whole set gives a complete new review revision whose earlier approval is dead; untouched items, omitted edit fields and a renamed workout's steps are kept, and finished changes survive a replacement.
Reject a stale or foreign approval: an access change or an external edit after review stops the approval before any write.
Change a reviewed target's duration from 60 to 90 minutes before approval → apply zero changes from the set.
Inspect the response to C01 → identify the workout, say it changed in intervals.icu, and explain the 60-to-90-minute difference.
Inspect the response to C01 → state that no changes were applied and present a refreshed review requiring new approval.
Separately change date, name, description, training load, and effort structure before approval → detect every review-relevant difference before the first write.
Change only unrelated server metadata or an equivalent normalized representation → keep the reviewed workout valid without an unnecessary new approval.
A deletion names its exact event and reviewed snapshot, deletes only that event, and a canceled review's old controls stay dead after a relaunch.

Cancel is saved before it is shown, survives a relaunch, writes nothing when it comes first, keeps every earlier success, and a raced approval and cancellation give one saved result that the shown outcome matches.
Edits and deletes reach only coach-created WORKOUT events dated today or later, and no add or move lands in the past, checked at preparation and again before the first write.
Date, name, duration, description, Load and structured effort reach the outbound request exactly as reviewed, and the desk sends each reviewed change as its own request.
A changed target stops the set before any write, names the difference and offers a refreshed review whose new approval runs it while the older approval writes nothing.
Each send attempt is saved before its request, a Receipt comes only from intervals.icu's answer, and the run stops at the first refused or unconfirmed change with successes shown apart from the rest.
Inspect the calendar after approval → preserve the unrelated 45-minute workout and every other untargeted workout.
Cancel before execution → apply zero changes and make the canceled approval unusable.
Propose edits and deletions of workouts without coach provenance → reject those actions without calendar writes.
Propose edits and deletions of calendar entries outside category WORKOUT → reject those actions without calendar writes.
Propose edits and deletions dated before the athlete-local current date → reject those actions without calendar writes.
Approve otherwise valid edits and deletions dated today or later → allow those actions under the existing restrictions.
Move a workout to a past date → reject the move without calendar writes.
Approve the refreshed eligible set → apply only the newly reviewed changes.
Fail a mixed set after two confirmed successful writes → stop before attempting subsequent changes.
Progress is saved before the next action, every send attempt is its own record, and a lost answer after a possible save is settled as uncertain, never replayed.
Authority is checked again at execution, and a review of one athlete writes nothing when the connection belongs to another.
Review and apply the mixed set: the old control of a revised or refreshed review writes nothing, and the approved set applies once.
Exact pending reviews and partial execution are restored after a relaunch.
Relaunch and device restart more than ten minutes later restore the review.
A partial failure is restored without replaying a finished change.
Before the first write of an approval or a Try again, the account and every remaining target are checked again, and any failure blocks the whole unstarted set.

Every approve, Try again and cancel control is bound to one revision, chat, account, action and state and is claimed durably before any request, so a replaced, consumed, canceled, foreign or wrong-action control writes nothing.
Try again runs only the remaining work, checked again first; a changed remaining target writes nothing more and gives a refreshed review, and a finished change is never sent again.
Remove coach provenance or change eligibility after review but before approval → reject the stale set before its first write.
Advance the athlete-local date so a reviewed mutation becomes invalid → reject the invalid set before its first write.
Approve with a replaced, canceled, consumed, or unrelated-chat approval identifier → apply zero changes through that approval.
Double-click approval or deliver the same approval concurrently → execute the approved set at most once.
Delete a target or make its fresh state unreadable before approval → apply zero changes and explain that the target cannot be verified.
Attempt the old approval after a refreshed review appears → apply zero changes through the old approval.
Retry the remaining work from D01 → revalidate the remaining changes before writing them.
Complete the retry from D01 → preserve the first two successes without replaying their writes.
Change a remaining target before retry → apply no additional changes and require a refreshed review of the remaining work.
Inspect the stale-retry explanation → preserve the success report and say no additional changes were applied.

Lost write results are resolved conservatively: an accepted change is settled by reading first, a lost create leaves no duplicate, an unresolved change stays explained, and an observed change or a missing delete target is never shown as a coach action.
A change accepted remotely and interrupted before its local record is reconciled by reading first.
A lost create answer leaves no duplicate workout.
An unresolved change stays explained, and nothing is retried blindly.
New conversation keeps a waiting workout review, shown once at the top as prepared earlier.
Every step form and bound is checked before any write, and no single-workout tool is left as a bypass of the review.
Recovery runs without the model, survives an interruption during writes, and runs at every return of the app to the front.
Storage is versioned, an upgrade keeps the meaning of what was saved, and synced visibility is not authority.
An upgrade with pending and completed work keeps the completed outcomes and never runs stale work, offline and then online.
Edits change only the named fields and target the right event, a pending item id is never taken for an event id, and the coach reads the pending set before a revision or a whole-set replacement.
Preparation that cannot finish offers no shortened set, keeps saved memory, and reports that the review could not be prepared, apart from saved but not verified.
One workout goes through the workout review, with approve and cancel, and nothing is written before approval.
The mixed request of two adds, one edit and one delete prepares one review of all four changes.
Make one easier → a complete new review revision that keeps the untouched changes, and the earlier approval writes nothing.
An unrelated topic while a review waits → the review stays unchanged and can still be approved.
A request that cannot be prepared whole → no partial review, and the athlete is told the review could not be prepared.
